html:
The Ch'orti' are a Maya people of eastern Guatemala, around Jocotán and Camotán in Chiquimula, and of nearby Honduras, where the ruins of Copán lie. In 1492 they were one of many Maya peoples living after the end of the great Maya cities.

Their language matters to scholars: it is the closest living relative of the language written in Classic Maya script, spoken in cities such as Copán over a thousand years ago. Spanish conquest came in the 1520s and 1530s. Today the Ch'orti' are mostly small farmers growing maize and beans on steep, dry hillsides, and they have suffered severe droughts and food shortages. Their western neighbours are the Poqomam.
